magnesium and calcium ions enhance the barotolerance of certain bacteria, including Streptococcus, by chemically specific interaction with the same processes that they affect.

magnesium and calcium ions enhance growth of compressed, glucose-fermenting cultures of S. faecalis ATTC 9790, and that this enhancement occurs by two distinct mechanisms, both related to acid inhibition of growth.

magnesium and calcium ions enhance the barotolerance of some strains of Streptococci and that this effect is related to their ability to reverse the potentiating effects of high pressure on inhibition of growth by low pH.

the effects of hydrostatic pressure on the growth of bacteria and yeasts in a variety of media and under a variety of environmental conditions.
the study of the effect of pressure on the physiology of microorganisms and the effect of pressure and other factors on the survival of microorganisms in the environment.
the study of barotolerant microorganisms, which can grow at high hydrostatic pressures, and their potential use in food preservation.

magnesium and calcium ions, at a concentration of 50 mM, enhance barotolerance by a specific chemical mechanism in a limited range of bacteria.
Mg++ and Ca++, but not Na+, K+, Sr++, Mn++ or Cl-, Br- or SO4- ions, enhance barotolerance in some streptococcs, in ribose-utilizing streptococccs under pressure, and in some chain-forming cocci.
Mg++ and Ca++, at a concentration of ca. 50 millimolar, enhance barotolerance in streptococcl, in some strains of chain-forming bacteria and in some yeasts, but not in E. coli or in S. cerevisiae.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
barotolerance of a variety of bacteria, and of yeasts, is enhanced by the presence of divalent cations in their growth medium.
barotolerance of a number of organisms can be enhanced by the presence of magnesium and calcium ions, but that the enhancement is not universal and that the mechanism is not yet understood.
